parallel.note: Documents were curated across 1 worker processes in 0.9 seconds. Small documents were read in the calling process, because handing one to another process costs more than reading it does. The order documents are reported in is the order they appear in data/raw, not the order they finished, so two raw files that curate to the same digest are reported the same way every run.

note: Architecture 25 lists conversations as a source. This corpus holds 0 conversational and 0 prose documents. Jupiter cannot learn to take turns from prose alone, and no dialogue is fabricated to fill the gap.
template_artifact_note: 1 documents were refused because they contain more than 5 chat-template markers such as [SYSTEM]:. That is a leaked conversation template, not dialogue, and a model trained on it emits instructions instead of conversing. The files in data/raw/ are untouched; they are listed under contaminated_documents so the owner can decide what to do with them.
structured_note: 0 of 200 accepted documents came from a structured source, providing 0 records of which 0 carried no field this pipeline recognises as text and were left out. An unrecognized record is a shape json_source cannot read yet; it is never guessed at, because invented text becomes training material nobody wrote.
unreadable_note: 0 structured files were refused. They are listed under unreadable_files with the reason, and the files in data/raw are untouched. Refusing is not deleting: the owner decides what to do.
unsupported_note: 0 files in data/raw carry an extension this pipeline does not read (.json, .jsonl, .ndjson are parsed, and .txt/.md/.text are read as text). They are listed under unsupported_files rather than passed over silently, because a file that is skipped without a word is a file whose owner has no way to know it is doing nothing.
oversized_note: 0 raw files were larger than max_raw_bytes (67108864 bytes) and were not read. They are listed under oversized_files with their size and the limit. Curation reads a whole document to judge it, so a file this large needs memory proportional to itself rather than to the context window Jupiter learns from. The files in data/raw are untouched: refusing to read a file is not deleting it.
retained_note: 10 curated files were kept even though their raw source is not in data/raw right now. Their digests were recorded by an earlier run, so this pipeline produced them from material it accepted. Their absence from raw means the corpus is being staged in batches; they are moved out only if a later run refuses the document itself.
unchanged_note: 200 of 201 files were already curated and had not changed since the last run, so they were not read again. A file is re-curated when it changes, when its curated output has gone missing, or when the curation rules themselves change.
